text:
alex: FYI I repro'd a perf regression on multi-GPU after the kernel-selector tweak landed. throughput ~12% down on our TP+PP tests, tail latency spikes occasionally. nvprof and an nsys timeline attached (summary pasted below).

sasha: which workload? batch sizes / seq len?

alex: tp=8, microbatch=2, seq=2048, kv-cache warm. Baseline (old selector) step time ~ 58ms, new selector ~ 65ms. Below are aggregated custom timers from the run: 
```
kv_read: 12.3ms
kernel_launch+compute: 9.2ms
allreduce (per-step): 6.7ms
ipc_wait/gpu_sync: 5.8ms
overhead (kernel selector): 3.1ms
```

jia: does the allreduce overlap look different in the timeline? any serialization points?

alex: yes — in the nsys timeline the allreduce windows appear more serialized across ranks after the selector change. Before we had staggered async-comms during KV-prefetch; now there are aligned bursts that cause PCIe saturation in places.

omar: hypothesis: the new kernel emits a different stream ordering (kernel on default stream instead of compute stream) which prevents CUDAGraph/stream-ordered allreduce overlap. Could also be a change in kernel launch flags (sync kernel).

sasha: can you paste the nvprof/nsys capture commands you used?

alex: ran two captures: `nvprof --print-gpu-trace --profile-from-start off --export-profile nvprof_old.nvvp ./run_repro.sh` and `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=nsys_new ./run_repro.sh` for the new commit. I also added lightweight micro-timers inside runtime: `timer.start("allreduce_start")`/`timer.stop("allreduce_end")` around the NCCL calls.

perf-bot: regression-alert: step-latency increase detected on commit abc1234 (impact: 11.8% throughput drop, triggered perf/regressions). Link: https://ci/internal/perf/abc1234

jia: can you paste the specific timer deltas between baseline/new for the allreduce and kv read?

alex: sure — aggregated over 500 steps: 
```
allreduce (baseline): avg 4.1ms, p95 5.9ms
allreduce (new): avg 6.7ms, p95 9.4ms
kv_read (baseline): avg 11.8ms, kv_read (new): 12.3ms
compute (baseline): 9.0ms, compute (new): 9.2ms
```

omar: so biggest reg is allreduce. If compute didn't change much but allreduce grew and lost overlap, it's probably ordering. Check stream indices in `cuLaunchKernel` events in nsys. Also verify NCCL version/hierarchical collectives didn't switch.

sasha: another quick repro: set `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=old` in env and rerun on the same machine, see if numbers return. If yes, bisect the selector change for the exact line.

alex: I did that — setting the env reverts perf to baseline within noise. So selector path is the culprit.

jia: next steps proposal: 1) capture a short nsys timeline with stream markers and per-thread names (use `cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(..., cudaStreamNonBlocking)` markers), 2) instrument NCCL calls with timestamps on host and device (GPUTimer) to see kernel vs comm ordering, 3) try forcing `cudaLaunchBelowStream`/change stream on the new kernel to see if overlap restores.

omar: +1. Also try `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` to see if any unexpected synchronization/coll-reductions are being triggered. If the selector inserts a small host sync (e.g., `cudaDeviceSynchronize()`), that'll fully break overlap.

alex: I can run the short nsys profile now and upload the .nsys-rep. I'll also add two fine-grained timers: `kernel_submit_time` and `allreduce_enqueue_time` to capture latency between kernel return and NCCL call.

sasha: assign an owner to the bisect? alex you started it, but ping me if you need help with kernel selector logic. I'll also check commit history around the selector for changes to stream usage.

perf-bot: note: add perf test `tp_pp_overlap_smoke` to CI with seq=2048 to catch regressions like this (added as RFC).

alex: ok I'll run the nsys capture and post the small timeline + the timers. Schedule a quick sync if we can't repro remotely. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: cheers — if you find kernel flags (sync vs async), paste that snippet. We can roll a patch to force non-blocking launches until selector is fixed.

alex: will do. thanks!
